userStories.title: Wire same-head re-runs into PR publish and record accepted re-runs
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Enable the same-head recovery adapter only for the workflow's own PR publish and carry accepted job names into outcomes, the feature record and ledger.

**Motivation** — The CI wait already re-runs GitHub jobs that never got a runner (`ci-starved.ts`, `rerunJob`), but nothing re-runs a job that failed on one pipeline and passed on another for the same commit, and nothing re-runs a GitLab job at all.

**Approach** — **Publish wiring (US-003).** A new module `src/workflow/ci-same-head.ts` exports:

```ts
export function sameHeadRerunFor(fc: FeatureContext, url: string, head: string): SameHeadRerun;
```

- `read()` is `_ciSameHeadDeps.readCiFailures(fc, { url, head })`, whose default is `readCiFailuresFor` (`src/workflow/ci-failures.ts`).
- `rerun(check)` resolves the PR once (`prNumberFromUrl(url)`, then `resolvePrRef` through `_ciFailuresDeps`) and, for a GitHub ref, calls `rerunJob({ host: ref.host, repo: ref.repo, jobId: check.jobId }, fc.projectDir, _ciSameHeadDeps.run)` from `ci-starved.ts`; for a GitLab ref it runs, through `_ciSameHeadDeps.run`, `glab api --hostname <host> -X POST projects/<encodeProjectPath(ref.repo)>/jobs/<jobId>/retry` and returns true exactly when the exit code is 0. A check without `jobId`, or a throw anywhere (including from `resolvePrRef` or `run`), returns false. `_ciSameHeadDeps = { run: CiRun, readCiFailures: typeof readCiFailuresFor }`, with `run` defaulting to `defaultForgeDeps.run` and `readCiFailures` to `readCiFailuresFor`, so no test touches a real forge or needs `mock.module`.

`waitForCi` (`src/workflow/finalize.ts`) gains an optional third parameter, the draft PR URL. `prMode` passes `draft.url` when the forge returned one, and `waitForCi` then passes `sameHeadRerun: sameHeadRerunFor(fc, url, expectedSha)` when `expectedSha` was read. `pushMode` passes no URL and gets no option (the caller owns that PR). `finalize.ts` is at 578 lines, so the URL and option plumbing must stay within its limit; helpers go in `ci-same-head.ts`.

`PublishOutcome` gains `ciReruns?: readonly string[]`, copied from `CiWaitResult.sameHeadReruns` by `ciDetailFields`, which already spreads the wait's detail into every outcome built from a CI wait. `publishStep` (`src/workflow/feature-steps.ts`) writes the ledger note `CI re-ran <names joined with "; ">: they passed on another pipeline for the same commit` (with `NO_MIRROR`) when `out.ciReruns` is non-empty, and patches `ciReruns: out.ciReruns` unconditionally, as it already does for `ciDetail`: the key is this publish's fact, so a publish whose wait re-ran nothing clears what an earlier publish recorded (the patch carries the key with value `undefined`). `WorkflowFeatureRecord` gains `ciReruns?: readonly string[]`, and the `publish` node in `feature-graph.ts` adds `"ciReruns"` to its `produces` list (the step graph rejects a patched key a node does not produce).

**Scope** — In: new sameHeadRerunFor adapter and injection seam, GitHub/GitLab retry requests, finalize URL/HEAD opt-in, shared CI outcome projection, feature record/graph registration, ledger note and stale-fact clearing. Out: reader evidence construction (US-001), wait eligibility and state logic (US-002), finding and prompt enrichment (US-004). `nax workflow promote` and `nax bot fix` CI waits: only the workflow's own publish (`prMode`) passes `sameHeadRerun`. Posting a PR comment about a re-run: the ledger note and the record's `ciReruns` are the record of it. Consolidating `rerunJob` (`ci-starved.ts`) into the forge module. Automatic retry settings in a project's own CI configuration (for example GitLab `retry: when: script_failure`): that is each project's choice.

**Interface** — Target `waitForCi(fc: FeatureContext, forge: ForgeKind, prUrl?: string): Promise<CiWaitResult>`. Target `ciDetailFields(ci: CiWaitResult): Pick<PublishOutcome, "ciDetail" | "ciReruns">`, with ciReruns present exactly when ci.sameHeadReruns is non-empty. PublishOutcome and WorkflowFeatureRecord retain every existing field and add optional `ciReruns?: readonly string[]`. Consume upstream SameHeadRerun and CiWaitResult.sameHeadReruns without redefining them. Existing forge helpers are `prNumberFromUrl(url: string): number | null`, `resolvePrRef`, `encodeProjectPath`, `rerunJob(job: ActionsJob, cwd: string, run: CiRun): Promise<boolean>`, ActionsJob and CiRun.

**Test implementation** — Create test/unit/workflow/ci-same-head.test.ts with _ciSameHeadDeps and _ciFailuresDeps fakes for reads, lazy cached ref resolution, exact host-aware commands and fail-closed results. Extend existing finalize and publish tests and feature-graph.test.ts. In finalize-ci.test.ts, replace the exact options comparison in "AC-9/15/16: publish waits for pushed HEAD with configured timeout, cadence and signal" for URL-bearing pr mode with the existing fields plus sameHeadRerun containing read/rerun functions; every option that existed before is passed unchanged. Add ciReruns to expectedProduces.publish in the exact node-shape test. Exercise publish(fc, input), call the captured read callback, verify PR number 9/head aaa through _ciFailuresDeps, and verify stubbed sameHeadReruns reaches PublishOutcome.ciReruns. Exercise publishStep for ledger options and own-key undefined clearing; do not conditional-spread the record patch.

routing.reasoning: New forge retry integration crosses adapter resolution, publish orchestration, outcome projection, graph patch ownership and persistence with lazy caching and fail-closed behavior; it does not change authentication or access control.

Replace the exact-object check for that case with the existing fields plus a `sameHeadRerun` with `read` and `rerun` functions; the invariant that replaces it: every option that existed before is passed unchanged.

the node-shape test asserts each node's sorted `produces` equals `expectedProduces[id]` exactly, and `expectedProduces.publish` has no `ciReruns`; add `"ciReruns"` to that list. The invariant that replaces it: the `publish` node's `produces` set equals the expected list exactly.

userStories.title: Give CI repair same-head facts and an explicit non-reproducible no-change outcome
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Enrich eligible repair findings with same-commit evidence and let the repair brief explicitly permit no change when that failure cannot be reproduced.

**Motivation** — For a failure that does not reproduce, editing something is the only move the brief describes.

**Approach** — **Facts for the repair (US-004).** `ciRepairPlan` / `readCiFailuresForRepair` (`src/workflow/ci-repair-steps.ts`) keep their gating and their single read. `ciCheckIssue` appends a facts paragraph to a check's issue text **only when the check has `passedOnSameHead`**, so every existing issue text is unchanged:

- always: `This check passed on another pipeline for the same commit` followed by ` (<url>).` when the fact has a url, or `.` when it has none;
- when `out.ciReruns` includes the check's name: `The CI wait re-ran it once before this repair round.`;
- when `rec.finalGates` exists, its `ran` list is non-empty and its `failing` list is empty: `The repository's own gates (<ran joined with ", ">) passed locally on this commit.`

The paragraph is separated from the existing text by one blank line and its sentences are joined by single spaces. `ciRepairPlan` takes the published outcome it already receives (`out`) and the record (`rec`), so no new parameter reaches it.

`buildWorkflowCiRepairPrompt` (`src/prompts/builders/workflow-ci-repair-builder.ts`) gains one exported constant, listed under "How to work" after `CI_REPAIR_STEP_REPRODUCTION_RULE` and re-exported from `src/prompts/index.ts` beside `CI_REPAIR_STEP_REPRODUCTION_RULE`:

```ts
export const CI_REPAIR_NON_REPRODUCIBLE_OUTCOME =
  "A check whose finding says it passed on another pipeline for the same commit may be non-deterministic: if you cannot reproduce its failure locally, change nothing for that check, reply DONE_WITH_CONCERNS, and say so, with what you ran, in concerns.";
```

It is an allowed outcome, not a new restriction: every existing rule in the brief stays, including `CI_REPAIR_NO_SHORTCUTS_RULE`. The `concerns` field the reply contract already carries is recorded by `ciRepairStep` into `ciRepairConcerns`, so the no-change outcome reaches the ledger and the approval advisor with no new plumbing.

**Scope** — In: conditional facts formatting in the existing repair-plan path, forwarding current outcome re-run names and record final gates to the private formatting helpers, exact prompt constant insertion and barrel re-export, and behavioral tests at publishStep and prompt entry points. Out: forge fact collection (US-001), wait state/re-run decisions (US-002), API/publish/persistence additions (US-003), new concerns storage or repair eligibility. Comparing the failing tests with the files the branch changed, or with the run-start test baseline: CI log excerpts are unstructured, so this would mean guessing test names from logs. Changing what a CI repair round does after a no-change outcome (it still returns to the final gates and publishes again, as today).

**Interface** — Preserve `ciRepairPlan(env: FeatureEnv, rec: WorkflowFeatureRecord, out: PublishOutcome, head: string | undefined): Promise<CiRepairPlan | undefined>` and its current gating/single-read contract. `ciCheckIssue(check: FailedCheck): string` and `ciRepairFindingsOf(checks)` both also take the facts they need (`out.ciReruns`, `rec.finalGates`); the text for a check without `passedOnSameHead` is unchanged. The existing `RepoGateSummary { ran: readonly string[]; failing: readonly string[] }` is declared in src/workflow/types.ts. Export the exact constant above from both its builder module and @/prompts.

**Test implementation** — Extend test/unit/workflow/feature-steps-ci-repair-decision.test.ts and test/unit/prompts/workflow-ci-repair-builder.test.ts. Enter through publishStep(env, rec) so the outcome, read checks and record really reach the repair finding rather than testing an isolated string helper. The common facts fixture is a draft outcome whose CI failed, a repair round left, and readCiFailures returning `{ name: "test", excerpt: "boom", passedOnSameHead: { url: "https://gitlab.com/g/p/-/jobs/601" } }`; out.ciReruns and rec.finalGates are absent unless the criterion changes them. Existing fixtures have no passedOnSameHead, so their exact issues stay unchanged; current brief tests use toContain and must retain every old rule. Do not add another failed-check read or alter ciRepairStep/noteConcerns control flow.

analysis:
Goal and completion: close #2969 by using forge evidence that a same-named check passed elsewhere on the identical head commit to attempt a bounded, token-free job re-run before starting repair. If recovery cannot be requested or fails again, preserve today's repair eligibility and provide the agent factual context plus an honest DONE_WITH_CONCERNS/no-change outcome. This is an enhancement to existing TypeScript/Bun workflow orchestration, not a new subsystem. All implementation belongs to packages/nax; no other workspace, dependency, release, configuration or credentials changes are needed. Execute the binding sequence US-001 -> US-002 -> US-003 -> US-004 with the exact declared dependency edges. Graph navigation tools were unavailable in this planning session; discovery used direct source reads and targeted searches. No code or validation commands were run for this PRD.

Repository conventions: docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:145-160 establishes the 600-line source hard limit, 800-line test hard limit, external-call _deps injection, named constants, type safety and injectable test sleeps. Read the architecture index and applicable .nax/rules before implementation. Source modules ci-wait.ts (580 lines) and finalize.ts (578 lines) have very little growth budget. Keep their additions as small plumbing calls and extract all new substantive decisions into the two specified new modules. Avoid import cycles: the established ci-wait-starved pattern uses only type imports back to ci-wait.ts. Use Bun-native runtime conventions and bun:test with command-keyed fake forge responses; never real forge calls, real sleeps or mock.module. Targeted tests run from packages/nax with explicit test paths, never bare bun test. The normal pipeline performs gates; do not make validation a separate story. Coverage is a separate outside-session concern, not an acceptance criterion or a reason to run coverage inside a sandboxed agent session.

US-001 current implementation: packages/nax/src/forge/ci-failures.ts:25 declares FailedCheck with name, optional URL, excerpt, logUnavailable and step metadata. MAX_FAILED_CHECKS is 5 at :38. Preserve these fields, excerpt redaction/bounding and existing filtering. PASSED_CONCLUSIONS at :45 treats success/skipped/neutral as non-failures, but evidence of a passing sibling must specifically require conclusion success. GithubCheckRun and normalization already retain id, name, conclusion, html_url and app slug (:109, :135). actionsJobId at :212 already constrains job ids to github-actions; reuse that result instead of treating all check-run ids as Actions job ids. toFailedCheck at :242 currently combines URL, logs and steps; readGithubFailedChecks at :250 currently filters and caps the parsed reply before converting. Retain all parsed runs long enough to find exact, non-empty name success matches before applying failed-check conversion; never infer a same-head fact from logs, skipped or neutral conclusions. The endpoint at :256 uses per_page=100&filter=latest. Its retention of same-name runs across check suites remains unverified, so preserve the existing query and accept no evidence/no re-run if GitHub collapses them.

GitLab normalization and parsing already tolerate missing numeric ids (:278-313), but findPipeline chooses the first matching sha (:317); do not change that selection. toGitlabFailedCheck at :322 currently drops the job id after reading its log. readGitlabFailedChecks at :340 reads MR pipelines, then the chosen pipeline's failed jobs, excludes allow_failure and missing-id jobs, caps them and reads traces. Add jobId to each returned GitLab check. Only after a non-empty failed-jobs read should up to three other same-sha numeric-id pipelines be probed, in reply order, for at most 100 success jobs each. Keep the chosen pipeline's failed-jobs read as the second forge call. Missing-id siblings consume no quota, different SHAs are never queried, and failed/malformed/non-array sibling replies lose only that sibling's evidence. Existing primary listing failures remain errors, unlike these new best-effort auxiliary reads. A name match may come from an unrelated workflow, an explicitly accepted bounded false positive. outOfScope: Comparing the failing tests with the files the branch changed, or with the run-start test baseline: CI log excerpts are unstructured, so this would mean guessing test names from logs.

Re-running a check more than once per CI wait, or re-running a failed check that did not pass anywhere else on the same commit: the re-run exists only for the case the forge itself shows to be non-deterministic.
Re-running a non-Actions GitHub check run (any app other than `github-actions`): it has no job endpoint, so it gets no `jobId` and its failure is repaired as today.
Choosing the GitLab head pipeline differently: the failed checks still come from the first pipeline whose sha is the head.
`nax workflow promote` and `nax bot fix` CI waits: only the workflow's own publish (`prMode`) passes `sameHeadRerun`.
Posting a PR comment about a re-run: the ledger note and the record's `ciReruns` are the record of it.
Changing what a CI repair round does after a no-change outcome (it still returns to the final gates and publishes again, as today).
Automatic retry settings in a project's own CI configuration (for example GitLab `retry: when: script_failure`): that is each project's choice.
